headlines.summary: Southern Co. (SO) closed at $87.04 in the latest trading session, marking a +1.01% move from the prior day.

headlines.title: Southern Company vs. NextEra Energy: One Stock Pulls Far Ahead on Sustainability
headlines.summary: Southern Company offers a bigger dividend check today, but NextEra Energy is quietly building a growth engine that could leave Southern's payout in the dust over a 25-year retirement. The gap between these two utilities is wider than most investors realize.

headlines.title: Southern Michigan Bank & Trust Thanks Outgoing CEO for His Service, Announces Search for New CEO
headlines.summary: The boards of directors of Southern Michigan Bancorp and Southern Michigan Bank & Trust, known collectively as Southern, expressed gratitude for the service of John Waldron, who has resigned as president and CEO of Southern, and announced plans to search for a new CEO.

headlines.title: Is Southern (SO) Stock Cheap Or About Right On Earnings?
headlines.summary: Southern has delivered a 5 year gain that many utility investors would be comfortable with, yet the recent share swings leave a simple question open. Is the current US$85.44 price adequately backed by the earnings the business is generating today and is expected to produce in the years ahead? Southern has returned 64.1% over 5 years, which puts real weight on whether that performance lines up with the strength and resilience of its earnings base.

headlines.title: Southern Linc public sector account manager Leslie Benton named to Alabama 9-1-1 Board
headlines.summary: Southern Linc, a subsidiary of Southern Company (NYSE: SO), announced that Alabama public sector account manager Leslie Benton was named to the Alabama 9-1-1 Board. The organization is Alabama's primary fiscal and technology agent for 9-1-1 and partners with local emergency communication districts. It administers a statewide 9-1-1 fee and a 9-1-1 voice and data system that uses emerging technologies.

description: The Southern Company, through its subsidiaries, engages in the sale of electricity. The company offers electric service to retail customers and wholesale customers; and energy-related products and services to natural gas choice markets. It also develops, constructs, acquires, owns, operates, and manages power generation assets, as well as battery energy storage projects; sells electricity at market-based rates in the wholesale market; and deploys microgrids for commercial, industrial, governmental, and utility customers. In addition, the company is involved in the distribution of natural gas in Illinois, Georgia, Virginia, and Tennessee; distributes energy and resilience solutions; and invests in telecommunications. The Southern Company was incorporated in 1945 and is headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia.
